chunks: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring, and made them testify about themselves, (saying): 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, we bear witness,' lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We were heedless of this.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Primordial Covenant (Al-Mithaq) in Surah Al-A'raf?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this verse (Ayat al-Mithaq) is foundational for the concept of Fitrah, positing that the innate recognition of God is an inherent, pre-existing truth rather than acquired knowledge. It underscores the theological principle that human accountability on the Day of Judgment is rooted in this primordial testimony, which Imam Ali and other Imams are seen as the perfect manifestations of. This covenant establishes the basis for the Imamate, as the Imams serve as the living proof (Hujjah) of the covenant made by all souls.
